primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Achondroplasia due to FGFR3 gain of function
mechanism: Constitutive gain-of-function signaling through FGFR3 inhibits proliferation and differentiation of growth-plate chondrocytes, impairing endochondral ossification while largely preserving intramembranous ossification.
vignette: A child has disproportionate short stature with rhizomelic shortening of the limbs, macrocephaly, frontal bossing, and a relatively normal trunk. Genetic testing identifies the common FGFR3 p.Gly380Arg pathogenic variant.
lead: Which of the following cellular effects most directly causes this skeletal phenotype?
correct: Excess inhibitory FGFR3 signaling that suppresses growth-plate chondrocyte proliferation
distractors: Loss of FGFR3 signaling causing excessive chondrocyte proliferation
Defective type II collagen synthesis causing primary failure of articular cartilage matrix formation
Loss of fibrillin-1 causing abnormal elastic-fiber microfibrils
Haploinsufficiency of SHOX causing isolated mesomelic limb shortening
distractor_notes: Achondroplasia is caused by FGFR3 gain of function, not loss; FGFR3 normally restrains growth-plate chondrocyte proliferation.
COL2A1 disorders can cause skeletal dysplasias but are mechanistically distinct from the constitutively active FGFR3 pathway in achondroplasia.
Fibrillin-1 defects cause Marfan syndrome, not an endochondral growth-plate dysplasia.
SHOX haploinsufficiency causes Léri-Weill dyschondrosteosis/Turner-associated short stature patterns, not the classic FGFR3 achondroplasia phenotype.
key_expl: FGFR3 is a negative regulator of endochondral bone growth. The classic achondroplasia variants produce constitutive receptor activation, exaggerating inhibitory signaling in growth-plate chondrocytes. Long-bone growth is therefore reduced, producing rhizomelia and disproportionate short stature.
objective: Explain achondroplasia as constitutive FGFR3 activation that suppresses growth-plate chondrocyte proliferation and endochondral ossification.
